title: ～のは～だ — “the one that ～ is …”
summary: A pattern that pulls one part out of a sentence to highlight it. A plain-form phrase + のは + the focus + だ, giving “the one who ～ is …” or “what ～ is …”.

patterns.gloss: Verbs and i-adjectives in plain form (作るのは母だ)
Na-adjectives take な (大切なのは健康だ)

body.p: To highlight “my mother” in 母が毎朝ご飯を作る, you say 毎朝ご飯を作るのは母だ. Here の stands in for “the person / thing / fact”.
Use it to answer who / what / which questions, or to make the key point stand out. It is close to ～ことは but の is more conversational.

examples.ja: 一番（いちばん）大切（たいせつ）なのは健康（けんこう）だ。
examples.romaji: Ichiban taisetsu na no wa kenkō da.
examples.tr: The most important thing is health.

examples.ja: 毎朝（まいあさ）ご飯（はん）を作（つく）るのは母（はは）だ。
examples.romaji: Maiasa gohan o tsukuru no wa haha da.
examples.tr: The one who makes breakfast every morning is my mother.

examples.ja: 窓（まど）を割（わ）ったのは弟（おとうと）だ。
examples.romaji: Mado o watta no wa otōto da.
examples.tr: The one who broke the window is my little brother.

pitfalls: Na-adjectives need な: 大切なのは, not 大切のは.
Put the highlighted part right before だ / です; keep that order.
